A0228.title: Robot Debug Interface Hardening
A0228.definition: Closing or encrypting production debug & maintenance interfaces, enforcing BLE provisioning authentication, removing vendor-SDK hardcoded credentials, and minimizing maintenance-port exposure to prevent attackers from gaining device control via debug channels.
A0228.description:
Robot debug interface hardening addresses attacks like Unitree UniPwn (CVE-2025-35027) that gain root via BLE provisioning command injection, hardcoded keys, or unclosed debug serial ports; it converges the attack surface on four layers. First, production environments disable JTAG/UART debug ports or enable strong authentication, preventing physical-contact attackers from getting a shell. Second, BLE provisioning interfaces enforce mutual authentication and per-device unique keys, removing device-shared hardcoded encryption keys. Third, vendor SDKs remove hardcoded credentials and backdoor services (e.g., CloudSail-style pre-installed remote access), scanned and cleaned before shipment. Fourth, maintenance ports minimize exposure, keeping only necessary maintenance functions with operation audit logs.

This measure works with A0109 (IoT strong authentication and default-credential change), A0117 (default-credential scanning and auto-remediation), and A0114 (IoT security-configuration enforcement).
A0228.limitation: Maintenance convenience conflicts with security; post-hardening on-site debugging needs extra authentication, raising ops cost; legacy devices whose firmware cannot be upgraded retain vulnerabilities; BLE provisioning authentication may affect first-time provisioning UX; some vendors resist removing backdoor services for remote-ops convenience.
